results.title: The impact of social support on quality of life in Chinese parents of ...
results.content: # The impact of social support on quality of life in Chinese parents of children with autism spectrum disorder: the mediating role of resilience. This study examined how resilience mediates the relationship between social support and quality of life (QoL) among parents of children with autism spectrum disorder (CWASD) in China. Participants completed the Social Support Rating Scale (SSRS), the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC, Chinese version), and the World Health Organization Quality of Life-BREF (WHOQOL-BREF, Chinese Version). Social support was positively correlated with resilience (r = 0.60, p < 0.01) and all QoL domains, with correlation coefficients ranging from 0.48 to 0.67 (all p < 0.05). Mediating effect analysis revealed that resilience partially mediated the effect of social support on QoL (β = 0.61, t = 4.55, p < 0.001; indirect effect = 0.21, 95% CI [0.06, 0.13]). This study reveals that resilience is a crucial pathway through which social support is translated into improved QoL for parents of CWASD.
